works.title: El tiempo por testigo... A Sevilla

position_in_era.primary_genre_lineage: cante jondo (Lebrijano) × flamenco-jazz piano (Dorantes) — family-circuit duet
position_in_era.geographic_locus: Lebrija / Seville (Peña-Perrate-Pinini-Bacán family line made literal)
position_in_era.historical_role: The performance event that closes the upward / family-root axis of the Orobroy episode. *Agua, Aire y Fuego* — featured on Dorantes' 2010 retrospective album *El tiempo por testigo... A Sevilla*, also featuring Nolasco — is the late-career duet of nephew and uncle, with Dorantes' piano accompanying El Lebrijano's cante. Lebrijano died in 2016, six years after this recording. The 34-year arc from *Persecución* (1976) to this 2010 duet is the family voice translated across two generations: cante hondo as concept-album poetry → cante hondo as piano-accompanied family ballad.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Released 2010 on *El tiempo por testigo... A Sevilla*, recorded live in studio with Dorantes' working trio (Dorantes piano / Francis Posé double bass / Javi Ruibal percussion). Track also features cantaor Nolasco. Album marks 20 years of Dorantes' career.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Dorantes (David Peña Fernández, b. 1969, Lebrija) and El Lebrijano (Juan Peña Fernández, b. 1941, Lebrija) are nephew and uncle — Lebrijano is the brother of Dorantes' father. Same Peña-Perrate-Pinini-Bacán Romani flamenco dynasty. The duet performs the genealogy that the rest of the upward axis of the map sketches abstractly.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: Sevillian / Lebrija family table — the dynastic Romani-flamenco circuit of Lebrija and Utrera, now staged as a recorded performance event rather than an inherited folkway.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Cante (Lebrijano voice) + piano (Dorantes) + double bass + percussion + secondary cante (Nolasco). The piano takes the role traditionally held by flamenco guitar — the methodological inversion of the entire Orobroy project performed inside the family.
